en.title: Longest Pair of Different Substrings with Equal Character Frequencies
en.description:
Two strings in which every character occurs the same number of times, but whose contents are not exactly the same, form a perfect anagram pair. Find the maximum length of two contiguous substrings of the original string that form such a pair; they may overlap, two positions with identical content do not count, and output −1 if no such pair exists.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: One line containing the string. 1≤length≤100000, lowercase letters.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 4, 3 and −1. In the first example bcac and cacb have length 4 and overlap, which is valid.
hints: Record each character's first and last positions, and whether it appears in two different runs of identical characters. For each character c that appears in multiple runs, the candidate is last[c]−first[c]; take the maximum, and return −1 if there is no candidate.
